facts.fact: The Federal Ministry of Health's strategic plan for 2022-2024 names DHIS2 in three strategic interventions: expanding the use of integrated DHIS2 through primary health care (1.C), starting the rollout of DHIS2 reporting at selected hospitals (2.I) and reporting through DHIS2 under an integrated, digitalised health information system (5.E).

The plan's monitoring framework names the Federal Ministry of Health's health information system unit (FMoH-HIS) as the body responsible for every DHIS2 indicator, and DHIS2 itself as their data source, with 2021 baselines.

The plan states that its costing exercise and resource mobilisation strategy are still to be done and names no budget line or funder for DHIS2; it gives no date for this, so the document's published year is used.

The plan's situation analysis lists as a strength that DHIS2 is used as the electronic platform for data collection and analysis at the locality level, alongside an integrated health facility report system for hospitals and primary health care; it does not say whether localities key from paper forms, and gives no date, so the document's published year is used.

The plan's monitoring framework, citing DHIS2, gives 86.40 per cent of selected hospitals as using DHIS2 in 2021 and a hospital-level DHIS2 reporting rate of 72.40 per cent; it gives no numerator or denominator and does not separate hospital tiers, speaking of secondary and tertiary facilities.

The plan's monitoring framework, citing DHIS2, gives the reporting rate at primary health care level as 46.90 per cent in 2021, the same figure it gives as the overall DHIS2 reporting rate, with targets of 60, 65 and 70 per cent; it is a rate of reports received, with no numerator or denominator, and the plan places DHIS2 data collection at locality level.

facts.fact: WHO's 2020 assessment states that in DHIS2 the data from the facility are entered at the locality level, the flow running from facility to locality to DHIS2, and that localities have staffing needs for DHIS2 data entry.

WHO's assessment states that the DHIS2 platform covers 144 of 189 localities in 17 states, Khartoum State joining in 2021, that only 122 of those 144 localities reported into it in May 2020, mainly for loss of internet connectivity, and that reporting rates through DHIS2 rose from 30 per cent of facilities in 2016 to 61.5 per cent in December 2018 and 64 per cent in May 2020.

WHO's 2020 assessment states that DHIS2 has not been implemented in most hospitals, for want of funding and infrastructure, and that facility data are entered at locality level; it names no facility tier as entering its own reports.

WHO's 2020 assessment states that DHIS2 is customised by a core team in the Federal Ministry of Health, under its health information system directorate, with advanced configuration and system administration mostly supplied by expert technical assistance; it says DHIS2 was adopted in 2014 to carry the integrated system.

WHO's assessment states that a focus of the 2019 Health Reform Plan is further integration of the health management information system on the DHIS2 platform, and that a national plan and vision for an integrated HMIS on DHIS2 exists, while the 2013 health information policy needs updating and there is no e-health policy or strategy.

WHO's 2020 assessment states that the printing and distribution of the registers and report forms the system rests on still depend on donor funding, and that a Global Fund-supported consultancy upgraded every DHIS2 instance at the National Data Centre and the ministry; the passages read name no domestic budget line, though they say the ministry is seeking a common investment plan for partner and domestic support of DHIS2.

facts.fact: The Global Fund's Inspector General found that results from health facilities are consolidated by hand and then entered in DHIS2 above the facility, by the states, which had included only 32 per cent of health facilities, generally because facilities reported late; DHIS2 then carried malaria indicators only, with TB and HIV planned for 2019 and 2020. The audit covered June 2016 to June 2018 with field visits in 2018 to 21 localities, facilities and hospitals in three states; no numerator or denominator is given for the 32 per cent.
The Inspector General states that DHIS2 was in use for malaria in almost all 18 states, Khartoum excepted, but not in their health facilities, as found by the audit of 2018.

The Inspector General states that DHIS2 was not used in health facilities in 2018, their results being consolidated on paper and keyed above them; registers and report forms were out of stock in 75 per cent of the facilities the auditors visited, of 19 visited for data.

The Inspector General states that Global Fund grant money was invested in rolling out the Health Management Information System on DHIS2 in 2015 to 2017; the audit names no domestic budget line for it.

The audit treats the HMIS on DHIS2 as the Federal Ministry of Health's: the ministry, principal recipient of the health systems grant since 2015, was to move malaria results onto HMIS/DHIS2 by June 2019 and to carry out a general review of the HMIS, and the states enter the data.
